1.title: Build the Right Thing: Product Engineering (Part 1) — Kent C. Dodds, EpicProduct.engineer
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Product engineers use customer discovery (The Mom Test applied live) and architectural understanding to decide which problems deserve engineering effort, with agents changing implementation speed but not the judgment call.

2.title: From Raw Documents to AI-Ready Data — Leo Platzer & Jeff Koss
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Data quality cleaning (deduplication, staleness detection, sensitive-data filtering) doubled RAG recall in a real 80K-document corpus, with specific numbers on how stale/duplicate data crowds out useful context.

3.title: The Transcript Looked Fine. The Call Wasn't. — Debugging Voice Agents, Arize
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: Voice agents fail in ways text transcripts hide — latency, interruptions, mishearing — and you need audio + trace + evals to catch them.

1.title: Cooking with Codex — Charlie Guo & Gabriel Chua, OpenAI
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Concrete patterns for turning ad-hoc agent requests into repeatable workflows with verifiable completion criteria, supervision points, and deterministic checks — shown through six named build examples (translation app, Q&A site, form builder, Python package with Rust backend).

2.title: How AI Agents Pay: Checkout in ChatGPT and Google AI Mode — Sam Parsons, PayPal
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Three payment flows for AI agents (ChatGPT Instant Checkout, Google AI Mode, MCP + external checkout) with tokenization constraints and integration points demoed end-to-end.

3.title: How Many Credentials Should Your AI Agent Have? Zero. — Jim Clark, Docker
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: MCP gateways as sandboxes for agent safety — zero credentials in each sandbox, one control point per task, progressive disclosure of tools based on intent.

1.title: From Vibes to Production: Evaluating and Shipping AI Agents That Work 201 — Laurie Voss, Arize AI
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Live walkthrough of diagnosing agent failures via traces, then using a coding agent to fix the root cause (missing price filter) and validate with regression evals.

2.title: What Is an Inference Engine, Anyway? — Charles Frye, Modal
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Traces a request through an inference engine (tokenization → scheduling → model execution → detokenization), showing how the scheduler becomes a bottleneck and how KV caching, speculative decoding, and CUDA graphs relieve it.

3.title: Your LLM Judge Is a Confident Liar: Building Better Verifiers — Browserbase
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: LLM judges on web agent benchmarks overstate success by 2x (74% vs 38%); the Universal Verifier cuts false positives from ~50% to near zero using task-specific rubrics and screenshot evidence ranking.

1.title: Harness Engineering: How to Build a Software Factory — Dru Knox, Tessl
1.author: AI Engineer
1.hook: Harness engineering breaks agent-powered development into inner/outer/meta loops with specific metrics (manual takeovers, human PR comments, PRs started without human) to measure autonomy, automation, and quality.

2.title: The Self-Improving OSS Agent Stack — Marc Klingen, Langfuse
2.author: AI Engineer
2.hook: Self-improving agent loop — traces + datasets + evals running offline, with AI proposing fixes and maintaining eval criteria while humans set direction; demo shows a changelog writer catching leaked internal jargon and back-testing improvements.

3.title: Research to Reality with Google DeepMind — Paige Bailey, Google DeepMind
3.author: AI Engineer
3.hook: Browser-based inference with Gemma 4 (2B–31B params), quantized for sub-1GB footprint; comparison of model size vs. deployment requirements across browser, mobile, and GPU.
